# Jones et al. (2021) — Recommendations to Advance Space Trusted Autonomy

> **External, not NASA governance.** Useful for comparison and vocabulary. It never establishes
> what NASA requires, and must not be cited as NASA coverage.

| | |
|---|---|
| **Publisher / owner** | Jones et al.; AIAA conference paper (AIAA Ascend), authors from NASA, Analytical Mechanics Associates, U.S. Space Force, George Mason University and Bryce Space and Technology; hosted on NTRS (NTRS record 20210017228) |
| **Kind** | Research / conference paper; recommendations from an interagency forum (not a directive) |
| **Status** | NTRS record: STI type CONFERENCE_PAPER, Distribution PUBLIC, no publication date listed. The paper itself is 27 PDF pages |
| **Where to get it** | `https://ntrs.nasa.gov/citations/20210017228`; PDF `https://ntrs.nasa.gov/api/citations/20210017228/downloads/AIAA_Recommendations%20to%20Advance%20Space%20Trusted%20Autonomy_FINAL.docx.pdf` (confirmed anonymously off-network, 2026-10-26). Quoted here sparingly |
| **Binds whom** | No one. The paper addresses "the Partnership community" (abstract, p.1) |

**What it is good for, relative to NASA's documents.** A plain-language, multi-agency statement of what "trusted autonomy" means and where the gaps were seen for space systems, with working definitions of autonomy, trust and trustworthiness. Useful vocabulary when a NASA document says "autonomy" without defining it (our reading).

**Key content for AI / machine-learning assurance.**
- Working definition of trust: "A property between an Assessing Agent (Trustee) and a system that is trusted by the Assessing Agent" (§III.A, p.3); "Trusted" means the system "has met the confidence threshold of the Assessing Agent" and "Trustworthy/Assured" means it "should meet" that threshold (§III.A, pp.3-4).
- Method: 54 preliminary gaps were aggregated into 11 Aggregated Gaps, which underpin three recommendations (Introduction, p.3; Summary, p.19).
- Recommendation 1 (anomalies): "future missions require the storage of spacecraft anomaly data and metadata", plus a pilot consortium to share operations data (§V.A, p.18).
- Recommendation 2: an "autonomy-literate community" of developers, operators and end users, by expanding operator education (§V.B, p.19).
- Recommendation 3: "safe and benign development and testing environments", including in-space testbeds, plus surveys of verification and validation tools and metrics (§V.C, p.19).

**Nearest NASA counterpart.** None directly. For autonomy and verification topics in NASA's own documents see `../documents/NPR_7150.2D.md` and `../documents/NASA-STD-7009B.md`; this paper is a recommendation set, not a requirement source (our reading).
